findings.F1: Among bars where 14-day RSI sat below 50, a longer unbroken run below 50 was followed by a lower 14-day excess return. Run length is entered as negative days, so a positive pooled slope means longer runs did worse. The pooled slope was +0.00357 per day (t = 3.21, n = 142 grid cases), with Spearman rho 0.19 (p = 0.027). It held in ETH (t = 3.17, n = 76) and in w13–w24 (t = 3.86, n = 73), but was weak in BTC (t = 0.92, n = 66) and in w1–w12 (t = 0.86, n = 69). The signs below are re-expressed from round 2, where the regression was run on the signed run length.
findings.F2: The below-50 run effect partly survives the coin's own 30-day return. With both in the regression, the run-length slope keeps t = 2.30 while the 30-day return has t = 0.04 (n = 110). Across horizons it is mixed: the 7-day slope is negative in the same sense (t = 2.38, n = 330) and the 28-day slope agrees with t = 1.70 (n = 65). The 21-day slope reverses sign (t = 1.09, n = 92), so the effect is not clean across horizons.
findings.F3: The tested reversal after long runs above 50 is not in the bars. The above-50 run-length slope on the 14-day excess return is +0.00093 (t = +1.20, n = 194), the opposite sign to the idea. The book lost on both coins: mean daily −0.00134 in BTC and −0.00060 in ETH, while holding the coins earned +0.00118 and +0.00137.
findings.F4: Short-term momentum is concentrated in calm markets. On a non-overlapping 3-day grid, the slope of the next 3-day return on the past 3-day return is 0.211 (t = 3.72, n = 524) in the lowest 20-day-volatility tercile. In the middle tercile it is 0.009 (t = 0.20), and in the highest it is −0.025 (t = −0.66).
findings.F5: The calm-market momentum has the same sign in every split I made. The low-volatility slope is 0.257 (t = 3.45) in ETH and 0.100 (t = 1.07) in BTC, and 0.155 (t = 1.91) in w1–w12 and 0.270 (t = 3.41) in w13–w24. A graded version, the vol-scaled 3-day return weighted by how low the volatility is, gives t = 2.59 (n = 1571). At 7 days the gradient is weaker: the low-volatility slope is 0.091 (t = 1.01) against −0.019 (t = −0.32) in the high-volatility tercile.

ideas.idea: In a coin, the lower its 20-day volatility of daily returns, the more its 3-day return continues in the same direction over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: In quiet markets a trader can follow the last few days' move, and should refuse to chase short moves when volatility is high.
ideas.name: calm-market short momentum

ideas.idea: The longer a coin's 14-day RSI has stayed below 50 without a break, measured in days up to the current close, the lower the coin's return over the next 14 days.
ideas.consequence: A long stay of RSI below 50 is a reason to stay short or out of the coin rather than to buy the dip.
ideas.name: RSI below-midline downtrend persistence
